name: Chicken Karahi
description: Pakistani chicken karahi with bone-in chicken cooked in a concentrated fresh tomato masala and finished with green chillies, coriander and plenty of fresh ginger.
ingredients: 1 kg bone-in chicken, cut into small pieces
1 tsp red chilli powder, or to taste
method: Pat the chicken dry. Heat the oil in a wide karahi or heavy pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in an uncrowded layer, working in batches if necessary.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and stir briefly until fragrant, then add the chopped tomatoes, crushed coriander, red chilli powder and salt.
Cook uncovered over medium heat, stirring and pressing the tomatoes as they soften. Add only a small splash of water if the masala begins catching before the chicken is cooked.
Continue until the chicken is fully cooked and tender and the tomatoes have reduced into a thick masala that clings to the pieces, with oil beginning to appear at the edges.
Add the slit green chillies and half the julienned ginger near the end and cook briefly so they perfume the masala without losing all their fresh character.
Taste for salt, scatter over the remaining ginger and fresh coriander and serve immediately with naan or chapati.
tips: Use a wide pan so the tomatoes reduce instead of steaming the chicken in a watery sauce.
Stir the masala regularly as it thickens; add water a tablespoon at a time if it starts to scorch.
Add the fresh ginger in two stages so some cooks into the gravy and some stays bright on top.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat until the chicken and masala are thoroughly hot, adding only a small splash of water if needed.
serving: Serve hot with naan or chapati, sliced onion and lemon wedges.
image_alt: Pakistani chicken karahi with reduced tomato masala, green chillies, coriander and fresh ginger
image_caption: Chicken karahi finished with a concentrated tomato masala, green chillies, coriander and ginger.
technique: Karahi gets its body from fresh tomatoes and reduction, not from a flour-thickened gravy. Use a wide pan, cook mostly uncovered, and let the tomato juices reduce until the masala looks glossy and clings to the chicken.
doneness_cues: The tomatoes should lose their raw watery look and collapse into a thick masala.
The masala is ready when it clings to the chicken and only a light sheen of oil is visible around the edges.
The thickest chicken pieces must be fully cooked through while still remaining juicy.
Fresh ginger and green chilli added near the end should smell bright rather than stewed.
mistakes: Covering the pan for most of the cook, which traps steam and can leave the karahi watery.
Adding water automatically even though chicken and tomatoes release their own moisture.
Using flour or cornflour to mimic reduction; it changes the characteristic texture.
Reducing very slowly after the chicken is already tender, which can dry the meat before the sauce thickens.
substitutions: Boneless thigh can replace bone-in chicken, but check it earlier because smaller boneless pieces cook faster.
Very watery tomatoes may need a longer uncovered reduction; firm, ripe tomatoes usually give better control than adding extra water.
Adjust green chilli at the finish instead of increasing red chilli powder if you want fresher heat.
reheating: Reheat in a covered pan over low to medium heat with only a small splash of water if the masala is very tight. Stop as soon as the chicken is hot throughout so it does not dry out.

faqs.question: Why is my chicken karahi watery?
faqs.answer: Usually the pan is too crowded, the tomatoes are very juicy, the lid trapped steam, or extra water was added. Finish uncovered in a wide pan and stir more often as the masala concentrates.

faqs.question: Does authentic-style karahi need flour to thicken it?
faqs.answer: No. The characteristic body comes from reduced tomatoes, chicken juices and cooking fat. Flour can make the sauce pasty.

faqs.question: When should ginger and green chilli be added?
faqs.answer: Use some during cooking if desired, but keep part for the final minutes so the aroma remains fresh.
